case.question: Can embeddings from a replacement model be treated as compatible merely because their vector dimensions match?
case.expected: No. Changing embedder requires compatible corpus/query embeddings, reindexing and threshold recalibration; equal dimensions alone are insufficient.

6. Configuration sensitivity and failure analysis

6.1 Discrete decision changes

The evidence threshold creates discontinuities. A best usable score of 0.29 refuses, 0.30 permits a warning answer
and 0.45 permits an answer under current settings. Raising the strong threshold to 0.70 while retaining weak=0.30
would map the three historical pilot scores to one answer and two warning answers. This is a deterministic replay of
recorded scores, not evidence of improved correctness.

A new generator changes conditional text behavior while fixed evidence scores leave the gate unchanged. An
embedding-model replacement changes retrieval geometry and requires compatible corpus/query embeddings,
reindexing and threshold recalibration. Matching vector dimensionality alone does not make embeddings from different
models comparable. The current vector(768) schema additionally requires a migration if the new dimension differs.

6.2 Segmentation experiment

Running the actual chunker over the three demonstration files produced three chunks at 800/100, 800/0, 800/200 and
1,200/100 characters. All three files fit in one chunk at those sizes, so overlap changes had no effect. At 400/0 the
corpus produced five chunks and 1,394 stored characters; at 400/100 it produced six chunks and 1,694 characters.
The default stored 1,396 characters.

These counts demonstrate segmentation and duplication effects only. They do not measure retrieval quality or answer
changes.

changes. The tiny corpus is poorly suited to testing overlap because it exercises little boundary splitting under the
default setting. A realistic corpus should include long procedures, multi-page tables and cases whose evidence
crosses chunk boundaries.

6.3 Distinguishing failure layers


 Layer Example failure Required evaluation


 Access control Cross-workspace task read Role-matrix and object-scope integration tests


 Retrieval Relevant answer passage not retrieved Labeled recall@k and exact-search comparison


 Answerability Related evidence lacks requested value Held-out unanswerable/contradiction set

Generation Adversarial deletion premise enters answer Claim support and injection-contamination review


 Action control Duplicate or unauthorized tool execution Approval races, crash recovery and privilege checks


 Memory Unsupported answer reused as a fact Frozen-memory ablation and source-revocation tests


The passing action-sequence assertion and failing generated-text example are compatible: application controls can
constrain tools while the model still produces unsupported language. Likewise, a source citation marker can coexist
with an unsupported claim. Evaluation should preserve these distinctions rather than collapse every outcome into one
“AI accuracy” percentage.

 A10 provenance.json Source/evidence hashes and source-state caveats


Appendix B. Minimal replication protocol

Use the existing local models and execute source/run_model_pilot.py. Its requests use two temperatures, two seeds,
three fixed cases and a per-model warmup, saving all outputs as JSON. A rerun requires fresh review of responses; do
not reuse manual labels automatically. Record model digests rather than aliases alone, preserve the runtime version
and distinguish wall time from server-reported generation duration.

For an end-to-end comparison, create an isolated workspace per variant, ingest an identical versioned corpus with one
fixed embedder, prevent prior generated memories from contaminating later trials and run the same questions through
the authenticated task API. A model-only generation pilot is insufficient to measure retrieval or authorization effects.

For an embedding comparison, rebuild the corpus embeddings and recalibrate on a development split before
evaluating the held-out questions.

7. Discussion

RQ1 is supported within the implemented scope: the project combines document ingestion, scoped retrieval, threshold
refusal and a persisted owner-approval report sequence. It does not demonstrate a general agent planner, complete
semantic verification or a downloadable reporting product. RQ2 yields evidence for selected local functional and load
properties, with substantial limits on production inference. RQ3 yields a concrete, reproducible example of text
variation and contamination under one changed model-temperature configuration, without establishing a general
winner.

For deployment, the most consequential improvements are provenance-aware memory, reviewable report content

bound to source versions, durable processing recovery and an evaluation set that separates retrieval relevance from
answerability and faithfulness. Capacity work should exercise a mixed workload with ingestion and generation,
increasing corpus sizes and sustained duration. Model routing or larger models should be added only with
measurements showing their benefit for that workload.

8. Threats to validity and responsible use

Internal validity is limited by missing historical revision/digest metadata, non-isolated local resources, sequential
stage/model order and differences between the native model pilot and application endpoint. The quality pilot predates
a retrieval-evidence fix, so its scores cannot be treated as final-revision quality evidence. New pilot prompts omitted

application memory to isolate supplied-evidence generation, which also limits ecological validity.

Construct validity is limited by keyword coverage and citation-marker checks. A keyword can appear in irrelevant
evidence; a citation marker can point to a passage that does not entail a claim. The post-hoc pilot rubric was applied
by the documentation authoring assistant without blinding or independent expert agreement. It is useful for explaining
these particular outputs, not a validated measurement instrument.

External validity is limited by a three-file synthetic corpus, a repeated AI load question, six calls per model-temperature
cell and only two injection trials in each cell. Neither zero observed API errors nor three complete keyword-hit fractions

generalizes to arbitrary users, languages, domains or workloads. No public deployment, field-user benefit study or
long-duration model soak was recorded.

Statistical validity is limited by single load stages and tiny model samples. We report denominators and raw values
rather than significance tests or population-level confidence claims. The 1/2 contamination count in one cell is not a
stable estimate of attack success probability. Token length and cache effects confound model latency comparisons.

The evaluation inputs are synthetic maintenance statements; no private operational corpus was needed for the added
experiments. The bundle omits environment secrets and database dumps and records a redaction in a copied
development log.

development log. Real deployments should review document ownership, retention, access revocation, model-host
trust and user reliance. Local inference and a confidence score do not establish regulatory compliance or factual
safety.

9. Conclusion and future work

The workbench demonstrates a bounded local RAG workflow with application-controlled workspace access and
human approval. Its retained benchmarks establish successful selected local checks and high throughput for a narrow
authenticated-read workload. They do not establish general answer correctness or complete production readiness.
The new fixed-evidence pilot shows why model and temperature changes require direct inspection: a correct factual
answer can still adopt an unsupported adversarial premise.

Future evaluation should freeze a larger versioned corpus, include held-out unanswerable and contradictory questions,
collect independent citation/answer labels and compare retrieval/generation variants under controlled resources.

3.2 Retrieval and evidence decision

A question is embedded and searched against chunks satisfying the workspace predicate and a non-deleted source
predicate. The default result limit is six. For a query vector q and chunk vector v_i, the recorded score is cosine
similarity, equivalently one minus the cosine distance returned by pgvector. Let U be the set of evidence items
matching the expected workspace and not marked revoked, and let s* = max(s_i for i in U).

 D(U) = REFUSE if U is empty or s* < 0.30
 ANSWER_WITH_WARNING if 0.30 <= s* < 0.45
 ANSWER if s* >= 0.45

The threshold function is deterministic. It does not estimate the probability of answer correctness. One high-scoring
passage is sufficient for ANSWER, even if the requested detail is absent or other passages conflict. Stale evidence
adds a reason string in the gate without reducing the score. Normal executor items are constructed after
workspace-scoped SQL retrieval; revoked/stale metadata is not comprehensively propagated.

For non-refused tasks, numbered evidence and up to three recent eligible memory items are sent to the generator. The
task path uses temperature 0.3 and a maximum output of 800 tokens. The system instruction asks for evidence-only
answers, [n] citations and rejection of instructions inside evidence. Returned source filenames are evidence metadata,

not a semantic certificate for every claim.

3.3 Bounded orchestration and approval

The task begins in PLANNING, enters RUNNING, executes document_search and proceeds to VERIFYING and
COMPLETED. Report-related keywords add report_generate, which pauses in WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL. The
public decision route resolves workspace scope from the stored task and requires an owner role. An approval claims
RUNNING under a task-row lock before resuming execution, preventing the second concurrent decision in the tested
path from executing the same transition.

The current report tool returns Markdown stored in a task step. A public report-download artifact is not exposed. The
schema and step vocabulary are broader than the active workflow: dynamic model routing, general DAG planning,

graph retrieval expansion and complete tool-execution auditing remain outside the demonstrated implementation.

3.4 Memory and residual trust

An ANSWER decision writes up to 500 characters of generated text into memory with verified=true, and later prompts
describe these items as verified facts. This flag reflects the retrieval gate, not independent verification. Thus an
unsupported generated claim can become later context. Source deletion also does not establish revocation of
historical answer memories. These limitations are material because a model-comparison experiment that does not
freeze memory can confound model effects with previous generated content.
